sections.h2: Where are the Gila County Recorder's offices?
sections.html:
The Gila County Recorder runs two public offices, one in Globe and one in Payson, one in the county seat and one in the largest town. Both offices list weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

OfficeAddressPhoneFax
GlobeGila County Courthouse, 1400 E Ash St, Globe, AZ 85501(928) 402-8740(928) 425-9270
PaysonTommie Cline Martin Complex, 707 S Colcord Rd, Payson, AZ 85541(928) 474-7139(928) 472-5346

The Payson office is closed on the fourth Tuesday of each month. The county names Wendy Mannigel-Smith as Recorder and Stephanie Johnson as Chief Deputy Recorder. Its stated mission covers recording, preserving and retrieving public records and keeping voter files current, so the same office that records a deed also handles voter registration.

sections.h2: What is Fraud Notify, and should a Gila County seller use it?
sections.html:
Fraud Notify is a free alert service offered through the Gila County Recorder's Office that sends you a notice any time a document is recorded in your name. The county promotes it as protection against property fraud.

It fits sellers well. If you own a vacant or inherited house in Gila County, a notification would tell you if someone files a deed or lien against it. Sign-up is handled on the county's Recorder page.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a document in Gila County?
sections.html:
Arizona's fee statute, A.R.S. 11-475, sets $30 for most recorded papers, $15 when the United States, the state or a local government party asks for the recording, and $1 a page for copies, with $3 more for a certificate and seal. The Gila County page this guide builds on lists the same $1 copy rate.

Ask the Recorder, or the title company that closes your sale, before you plan around either.

sections.h2: Which Arizona transfers skip the affidavit of legal value?
sections.html:
A.R.S. 11-1134 lists instruments and transfers that do not need the buyer and seller affidavit, and the deed must say on its face which exemption is claimed. For Gila County families, several of these come up often.

  • A deed of gift.
  • A quitclaim deed executed for no money.
  • A conveyance made under a court order.
  • A lease or easement of any length.
  • A deed that confirms or corrects an earlier recorded deed.
  • A trustee's deed under a deed of trust, and transfers made only to secure or release a debt.
  • A transfer of residential property for only nominal consideration between spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, or siblings.
  • A transfer made under a beneficiary deed for only nominal consideration.
  • A sale for delinquent taxes or assessments, a partition, or a transfer made because of a legal name change.

An ordinary arm's-length sale of a Gila County house to a buyer is not on this list, so the affidavit is required. It states the price, the financing, the parcel number and the buyer's plans for the house.

sections.h2: What makes the Gila County Recorder reject a document?
sections.html:
Under A.R.S. 11-480 a recorder can turn away an instrument only if it lacks a caption, is not an original, is illegible, lacks original signatures, or is larger than 8.5 by 14 inches or set in type under ten point. Keep a two inch top margin on page one for the recording stamp, and half inch margins on the sides and bottom.

If an instrument modifies an earlier one, it must state the recording date and the docket and page of the earlier document. Where a first page fails the top margin test, a cover sheet carrying the document title can fix it.

sections.h2: Which Gila County communities file through these offices?
sections.html:
Gila County has six incorporated places: Globe, Miami, Payson, Star Valley, Hayden and Winkelman. The county sits in the Payson micropolitan area, which belongs to the larger Phoenix-Mesa combined statistical area.

  • San Carlos: 4,038 people in 2010.
  • Central Heights-Midland City: 2,534.
  • Pine: 1,963.
  • Claypool: 1,538.
  • Tonto Basin: 1,424.

The first five are unincorporated census-designated places, and recording for them runs through the same county Recorder as the towns do.

sections.h2: What happens if an affidavit is incomplete or a lender sells after foreclosure?
sections.html:
Under A.R.S. 11-1133 the recorder must refuse a deed or sales contract whose affidavit is incomplete, unless the paper notes a legal exemption. An affidavit counts as complete when every item is answered or marked not applicable.

A separate rule covers foreclosures. If the beneficiary of a foreclosed trustee's deed gets an extra payment from private mortgage insurance, it must file a declaration with the County Recorder within four months of the trustee's sale. The declaration lists the parcel number, the beneficiary, the sale date, the highest bid, the recording number and the extra amount received within three months.

If you are selling a house that has a foreclosure in its chain of title, this is background your title company will already know.

sections.h2: What is Gila County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Gila County covers 4,795 square miles in central Arizona. It was formed on February 8, 1881 from parts of Maricopa and Pinal counties, and the first seat was the mining town of Globe. Payson, the largest town, had 15,301 people in 2010, ahead of Globe at 7,532 and Star Valley at 2,310.

MeasureFigure

Population estimate, 202553,801

That vacancy figure is high. With nearly a third of units empty at the 2020 count and an older population, Gila County has many houses that sit unoccupied for stretches, and those owners may not see mail or recorded filings right away.

sections.h2: How do roads, land and schools affect a Gila County sale?
sections.html:
U.S. 60 and U.S. 70 cross the county, along with state routes 87, 260, 188, 77, 73, 177 and 288. Public-use airports are at Payson and near Globe. Parts of the Fort Apache and San Carlos reservations lie in the county, and so do portions of Tonto National Forest and Coconino National Forest and Tonto National Monument.

Ask a title company early about a parcel that sits close to public or tribal land, because access and ownership questions can slow recording. The unified school districts are Globe, Hayden-Winkelman, Miami, Payson, San Carlos and Whiteriver, and Pine Strawberry, Tonto Basin and Young run elementary districts.

Gila County also holds the towns of Miami, Hayden and Winkelman, with Hayden and Winkelman partly in Pinal County. A Hayden or Winkelman address may fall under either county, so check the parcel's county before you contact an office.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Gila County?
faqs.a: You can record at the Gila County Recorder's office in Globe, in the courthouse at 1400 E Ash St, or in Payson at 707 S Colcord Rd. Both list weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Is the Gila County Recorder's Payson office open every weekday?
faqs.a: No. The Payson office is closed on the fourth Tuesday of each month, according to the county's Recorder page. Call (928) 474-7139 before you go.

faqs.q: What is the copy fee at the Gila County Recorder?
faqs.a: Copies cost $1 per page. State law also adds $3 for the recorder's certificate and seal on a certified copy.

faqs.q: Do I need an affidavit of legal value to record a gift deed in Gila County?
faqs.a: No. A deed of gift is exempt under A.R.S. 11-1134, but the deed has to state the exemption on its face. A title company can confirm that for your situation.

faqs.q: Can I get alerts when something is recorded against my Gila County property?
faqs.a: Yes. The Gila County Recorder's Office offers a free Fraud Notify service that sends a notice any time a document is recorded in your name.
